title: Resident daemons — detecting stale running code and reloading without losing in-flight work
summary: Grounds decision #3681 (epic #3383): how this system's own long-running daemons (the conveyor runner and supervisor, the review / fix-dispatch / verify / pass daemons, the plateau-app drain daemon) should notice that the code they loaded is stale and pick up new code. Grounding: nothing records the commit a daemon booted from and nothing compares it to HEAD; the existing 'stale' checks cover a checkout (assertMainNotStale), a ref (main-ref-sync, prototype) or liveness (driver-watchdog), never the loaded code; in-flight state (detached claude --bg agents, file leases, persisted bookkeeping on the prototype, GitHub for the drain) already lives outside the process. Prior art converges: every production system except Erlang/OTP reloads by stopping at a safe point and letting a supervisor relaunch fresh code (systemd/launchd KeepAlive, Kubernetes rolling updates with preStop, nginx/Unicorn re-exec, pm2 reload); Node ESM cannot unload modules, so cache-busting hot-reload leaks module graphs and leaves old timers and closures running; staleness is detected by publishing the running revision (Prometheus build_info) and comparing it to the desired one (Argo CD / Flux OutOfSync); file watchers fire mid-checkout and cannot see an un-pulled origin. The ratified #2501 drain-daemon statute already applies this pattern to one daemon (dedicated clone + clean exit + KeepAlive relaunch between passes). Recommended ruling (after a skeptic round): generalize the reload — record per-repo boot shas and the files each daemon actually loaded (a runtime module-loader hook, since the runner and drain use lazy and cross-repo dynamic imports), check at each safe point whether any changed (with an age backstop), and exit cleanly for relaunch; a reload exit gets its own clean reason so the supervisor does not count it as a crash. Drift against origin is detected read-only and reported; self-updating a checkout is a per-daemon opt-in only where four conditions hold (review-gated branch, operator state outside the clone, a watchdog last-known-good pin, git clean spares state) — the skeptic refuted 'every daemon self-updates its own clone' (it splits the runner from the primary-writable queue, undoes watchdog rollbacks, and would self-apply unreviewed POC-branch code). Report: reports/2026-09-23-daemon-lifecycle-staleness-reload-prep.md.
